Rather than approving an initiative's full budget at the outset, it is funded stage by stage, with each stage's funding tied to passing its gate. Gompers showed that venture capital firms rely on this approach because it preserves their ability to review and stop, and that they shorten the interval between funding rounds as uncertainty increases (Gompers, 1995). The logic of real options explains why: a small investment at an early stage is like buying an option that allows the organization to invest more if the opportunity materializes, or to stop with a limited loss if it does not (McGrath, 1999). Amabile and her colleagues developed an instrument for assessing the work environment for creativity and used it to compare projects rated as high and low in creativity within the same organizations. In the thinking stage, a person needs freedom to explore, time to reflect, and as little premature judgment as possible. In the practice stage, the need changes: the idea now requires an opportunity to be tried in a real setting, enough resources to test it, and support from people who hold the authority or the expertise. Many organizations do one of the two stages well and neglect the other: competitions and hackathons celebrate thinking and then leave the winners with no route to practice. This is consistent with Baer's finding that creative ideas get implemented when their originators have both the motivation to implement them and a network of relationships to help them do so (Baer, 2012). The finding also matches what the Saudi innovators in the study cited above described: they all agreed on the importance of interacting with peers, and eight of them saw their network of relationships as a route to opportunities. Eight of them likewise held that turning the innovation into a source of income early on is a condition for persisting, and one recounted how a talented friend, forced into a job far from his passion, lost interest in his project (Alsamani, 2023). In the practice stage, then, resources do more than allow the idea to be tried; they determine whether the innovator will stay on the path.
